model: Apex with Panasonic display, 4109 software (Universal Gateway)
applies_to: Thermal Solutions Apex boilers with the control and Panasonic GT02 display running 4109 software, connected through the Universal Gateway.
summary: Apex boilers with the Panasonic display and 4109 software are read over Modbus RTU by the Thermal Solutions Universal Gateway (a ProtoNode) and served as BACnet IP or BACnet MS/TP devices. The 28-object profile has a burner on/off command, writable CH, DHW, lead lag and CH time-of-day setpoints, setpoint sources, sensor temperatures, burner state, lockout and hold codes, and cycle counters.
default_device_instance: 50000 + boiler Modbus address (BACnet IP and MS/TP multiple node); Node_Offset default 50,000
notes: The Universal Gateway is a ProtoNode (BACnet RER FPC-N34-0816, LonWorks LER FPC-N35-0817) that auto-discovers up to 8 boilers on its Modbus RS-485 port.
Every boiler is its own BACnet device with the same object list; the instances here are for one boiler.
Power all boilers and connect them before running auto-discovery; a boiler added later is not found until discovery is run again.
All writable values on this control are stored in EEPROM; write only when a value has to change, never cyclically.
Check the software version with the i button on the home screen: 4716 software uses a different list.

integration.summary: Give each Apex a unique Boiler Address (Adjust > Sequencer Slave), disable Sequencer Master on every boiler, wire the RJ45 boiler-to-boiler port to the gateway, run auto-discovery, then use BV 1 Burner On Off and AV 3 CH Setpoint. Values go to EEPROM, so write them only when they change.

minimum_points.name: Burner On Off
minimum_points.why: Burner enable from the BMS (1 = on)

minimum_points.name: CH Setpoint
minimum_points.why: CH setpoint, 79-191 °F; EEPROM, write on change

integration.enable: BV 1 Burner On Off enables or disables the burner. If only BV 1 is used instead of the boiler's Enable/Disable contact, the boiler stops but the system pump may keep running. For lead/lag, Enable/Disable and the remote firing rate (4-20 mA) must be hard-wired to each boiler, and the Sequencer must be disabled (no master boiler) while the EMS is connected.
integration.remote_sensors: When the BMS writes AV 3 CH Setpoint it takes over the boiler's CH setpoint, so disable the boiler's outdoor air reset. There is no writable outdoor or header temperature input.
setup: BACnet IP and MS/TP multiple node: each boiler is its own device, instance = Node_Offset (default 50,000) + boiler Modbus address, so address 1 = 50001.
BACnet MS/TP single node (for front ends without virtual-node support): one device at Node_Offset + MAC, with boiler objects renumbered 1001, 1002... for address 1, 2001... for address 2.

S-bank DIP switches pick the protocol (S0-S2 all Off = BACnet IP, S0 On = MS/TP multiple node, S2 On = MS/TP single node); S3 On at power-up runs auto-discovery (about 3 minutes), then set S3 Off to keep the configuration.
MS/TP MAC address 1-127 on A-bank DIP switches (one MAC for the whole gateway); baud rate on B-bank switches.
Change the IP address and Node_Offset in the ProtoNode web configurator (default IP 192.168.1.24).
Apex with Panasonic GT02: set a unique Boiler Address under Adjust > Sequencer Slave and disable Sequencer Master on all boilers.
gotchas: All writable parameters live in EEPROM: avoid repeated or cyclic writes.
Disable outdoor air reset on the boiler when the BMS writes the CH setpoint.
Boiler sequencing (lead/lag) must be done outside the boiler controls when the EMS is connected.

source.title: Thermal Solutions Universal Gateway Instruction Manual

points.name: Demand Source
points.description: Source of the current heat demand
points.states: 0=Unknown, 1=No source demand, 2=Central heat, 3=Domestic hot water, 4=Lead Lag slave, 5=Lead Lag master, 6=CH frost protection, 7=DHW frost protection, 8=No demand (burner switch off), 9=DHW storage, 11=Warm weather shutdown

points.name: CH Setpoint Source
points.description: What sets the active CH setpoint
points.states: 0=Unknown, 1=Normal setpoint, 2=TOD setpoint, 3=Outdoor reset, 4=Remote control (4-20 mA), 7=Outdoor reset time of day

points.name: DHW Setpoint Source
points.description: What sets the active DHW setpoint
points.states: 0=Unknown, 1=Normal setpoint, 2=TOD setpoint, 5=DHW tap setpoint, 6=DHW preheat setpoint

points.name: LL Master Setpoint Source
points.description: What sets the lead lag master setpoint
points.states: 0=Unknown, 1=CH setpoint, 2=CH TOD setpoint, 3=Outdoor reset, 4=Remote control (4-20 mA), 5=DHW setpoint, 6=DHW TOD setpoint, 7=Outdoor reset time of day, 8=Mix setpoint

points.name: Burner Control State
points.states: 0=Initiate, 1=Standby Delay, 2=Standby, 3=Safe Startup, 4=Prepurge - Drive to Purge Rate, 5=Prepurge - Measured Purge Time, 6=Prepurge - Drive to Lightoff Rate, 7=Preignition Test, 8=Preignition Time, 9=Pilot Flame Establishing Period, 10=Main Flame Establishing Period, 11=Direct Burner Ignition, 12=Run, 13=Postpurge, 14=Lockout

points.name: Lockout Code
points.states: 0=No lockout, 4=Supply high limit, 5=DHW high limit, 6=Stack high limit, 12=Flame detected out of sequence, 18=Lightoff rate proving failed, 19=Purge rate proving failed, 20=Invalid safety parameters, 21=Invalid modulation parameter, 22=Safety data verification needed, 23=24VAC voltage low/high, 24=Fuel valve error, 25=Hardware fault, 26=Internal fault, 27=Ignition failure

points.name: Hold Code
points.states: 0=None, 1=Anti short cycle, 2=Boiler safety limit open, 3=Boiler safety limit open (ILK off), 7=Return sensor fault, 8=Supply sensor fault, 9=DHW sensor fault, 10=Stack sensor fault, 11=Ignition failure, 13=Flame rod shorted to ground, 14=Delta T inlet/outlet high, 15=Return temp higher than supply, 16=Supply temp has risen too quickly, 17=Fan speed not proved, 23=24VAC voltage low/high, 25=Hardware fault, 27=Ignition failure
